short_summary: This article provides a comprehensive review of advanced strategies for creating biomimetic scaffolds that mimic the native extracellular matrix (ECM) for tissue engineering and drug development. It details the ECM's biological role and tissue-specific properties that guide scaffold design. Key fabrication techniques, including decellularization, electrospinning, and multidimensional bioprinting, are analyzed for creating natural, synthetic, and hybrid scaffolds. These scaffolds are applied in regenerating tissues like bone, skin, and cartilage, and in developing physiologically relevant 3D tumor models for more predictive drug screening. The text also addresses critical challenges such as achieving mechanical competence, ensuring immune compatibility, and establishing manufacturing standardization. It provides a holistic framework for researchers, covering design, fabrication, validation, and clinical translation, bridging the gap between laboratory innovation and therapeutic application.
long_summary: This comprehensive review details the design and application of biomimetic scaffolds that mimic the native extracellular matrix (ECM) for tissue engineering, regenerative medicine, and drug development. It begins by deconstructing the native ECM, emphasizing its tissue-specific biochemical composition (collagens, GAGs, growth factors) and mechanical properties (stiffness, viscoelasticity) that regulate cell behavior through mechanotransduction. The article provides an in-depth analysis of scaffold fabrication methodologies, including decellularization techniques to create natural ECM scaffolds, electrospinning for nanofibrous architectures, and multidimensional (3D/4D) bioprinting for creating complex, patient-specific constructs. A comparative analysis of natural, synthetic, and advanced hybrid scaffolds is presented, highlighting their respective advantages in bioactivity and mechanical tunability. The review explores key applications, such as regenerating tissues like bone, skin, and cartilage, and creating advanced 3D tumor models that better recapitulate the in vivo tumor microenvironment for more predictive drug screening. It also addresses significant challenges in the field, including enhancing mechanical strength, ensuring immune compatibility, and overcoming hurdles in manufacturing scalability and clinical standardization. The document serves as a technical guide, offering detailed experimental protocols and validation frameworks to bridge the gap between laboratory research and clinical translation.
